findings.summary: The mistakes list is a set of bare fragments with no heading and no fix.
findings.evidence: "File bytes through app servers / Trusting client-supplied hashes / Wall-clock time for versions / Deleting a block before verifying refcount / Polling every second instead of notifying"
findings.fix: Add a "Common mistakes" heading and a table with columns "Mistake" and "Do instead", as page 12 does.

findings.summary: Out-of-scope items are mixed into the functional-requirements list with no marker.
findings.evidence: "Version history with restore", "Real-time co-editing (OT/CRDT)", "Full-text search", "Media transcoding" appear in one run before "Files up to 50 GB..."
findings.fix: Split into two labelled groups, "In scope" and "Out of scope", or put them in a two-column table.

findings.summary: The 'Data plane rules' list holds unrelated client-agent bullets, and one table cell mixes two ideas.
findings.evidence: "Data plane rules" includes "Sync agent keeps a local SQLite DB..." and "Change detection uses OS file events, not scanning"; the table row says "Load | 12K QPS avg | Bytes skip app servers".
findings.fix: Move the SQLite and file-event bullets under a "Client agent" heading. Make the Load row compare like with like, e.g. "12K QPS of small requests" vs "bulk bytes, ~3.7 Gbps avg".

findings.summary: The schema uses a TEXT[] array column, which MySQL does not support, but the chapter names MySQL/Postgres as the metadata store.
findings.evidence: chunk_hashes TEXT[] in file_version (also version.chunk_hashes[] on page 6) versus 'Sharded SQL (MySQL/Postgres)' on page 3
findings.fix: Say the schema is PostgreSQL-specific, or store the block list in a child table (file_id, version, idx, hash) or a JSON column so it works on MySQL too.

findings.summary: The hot-shard fix seems to contradict the 'one namespace on one shard' rule.
findings.evidence: "Shard by namespace_id: one user's tree lives on one shard / Listing and move need no cross-shard join" vs "Hot shard (1M-file team folder) | Split by sub-tree"
findings.fix: Add one line saying that splitting a hot namespace by sub-tree is the exception, and that it makes moves across the split cross-shard.

findings.summary: The same 'which chunks are missing' step is named with a different endpoint on three pages.
findings.evidence: Page 1 and 4: "POST /chunks/missing"; page 7: "POST /uploads/init  send the hash list"; page 3: "Ask metadata which hashes are missing?"
findings.fix: Pick one name for the step. For example, show /uploads/init as creating the session and calling /chunks/missing, or use one endpoint on every page.

findings.summary: The GC rule is called 'two checks' but the list below it has three conditions.
findings.evidence: Diagram: "Two checks then delete block"; list: "Refcount is 0 / A scan of live manifests finds no reference / 7-day grace period has passed". Page 12: "a block is deleted only after two checks".
findings.fix: Say "three conditions" everywhere, or define the two checks (refcount 0 and no live manifest) and call the 7-day grace a separate wait.
